items.question_en: A wave is represented by the equation y = (0.02 m) sin(5πx − 20t). The minimum distance between the two particles always having the same speed is. (Assume x and t are in SI units)

solution.approach: Two particles have the same speed at every instant only if their phases differ by a whole multiple of π, and the smallest such separation is half a wavelength.

steps.text: Find the particle velocity by differentiating the displacement with respect to time.
Find the wavelength from the coefficient of x.
State when two particles keep the same speed magnitude for all time. Their phases differ by Δ, and |cos(θ+Δ)| = |cos θ| for every θ only when Δ is a whole multiple of π.
steps.why_this_step: cos(θ+Δ) reduces to ±cos θ for every θ only when sin Δ = 0, which needs Δ = nπ.

steps.text: Take the smallest nonzero multiple of π and convert it to a distance using Δ = k(x₁ − x₂).
steps.equation: Δ = π = k·d, so d = π/k = λ/2

common_mistakes.text: Reading off the amplitude 0.02 m from the equation and mistaking it for the required distance.
Requiring the velocity to match in direction as well as magnitude, which needs a full wavelength separation, giving 0.4 m.
Multiplying the wavelength by 2 instead of dividing it by 2, giving 0.8 m instead of 0.2 m.
